subject: NexusHealth: proposed tiered notification windows and evidence-access process
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@nexushealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana.lee@counselfirm.com>
Date: 2027-09-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Request: tailored notification windows + evidence access for NexusHealth

Hi Michael,

Quick context: NexusHealth is finalizing our DPA addendum and we need to clarify incident notification obligations and evidence access. Our security & legal teams are looking for two things we haven't seen in the standard Redwood DPA:

1) Tiered notification windows by severity and data category (e.g., PHI/PII vs. non-sensitive metadata) rather than a flat 72-hour window. We want to propose 24h for Critical (live exfil of PHI), 48h for High, 72h for Medium.

2) A documented process for direct evidence access: in certain incidents we require that NexusHealth's security team be provided with a forensically sound snapshot or exported logs under NDA so we can run parallel analysis. We understand there are operational constraints and privacy concerns, but we need a clear timeline (for delivery of sanitized evidence) and controls for cross-border transfer.

Can Redwood commit to a tiered notification approach and a narrowly scoped evidence-sharing workflow (not full disk images, but preserved logs and memory captures where feasible) under an NDA? Also please confirm how subprocessors will be looped in — will Redwood require subprocessors to cooperate in the same timeframes?

I've attached our intake form (Nexus_Req_Form.pdf) with examples of the artifacts we typically request.

We'd like to get alignment before we exchange final redlines.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Carter
Lead InfoSec Program Manager, NexusHealth
security@nexushealth.com

Attachment: Nexus_Req_Form.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tailored notification windows + evidence access for NexusHealth

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the intake form.

Short answer: we can discuss tiered windows and limited evidence sharing, but I want to set expectations up front so we land on an operationally deliverable clause. Our standard DPA references a 72-hour notification requirement for incidents affecting Personal Data and includes cooperation obligations with reasonable assistance from subprocessors.

Questions/notes:
- Can you confirm whether NexusHealth requires the tiering to be by data category (PHI vs PII) or by impact severity only?
- For evidence, we typically provide preserved logs, relevant service-side traces, and sanitized request/response samples. Full-forensic disk images or raw memory dumps are usually restricted due to third-party infra and privacy concerns.
- Cross-border transfer: we enforce our standard export controls and will only provide raw artifacts if legal review and any necessary DPA addendum language are in place.

I've attached an excerpt of the current DPA language for the incident notification & cooperation sections so we're all working from the same base. Laura and Neha: can you review and propose redlines for the tiered windows + evidence-sharing commitments?

Best,
Michael Grant

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Alex Carter <alex.carter@nexushealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tailored notification windows + evidence access for NexusHealth

Michael / Alex — looping in legal/privacy. Below is a proposed approach we can commit to operationally, with recommended clause language. High-level: we can agree to tiered notification windows with strict conditions, and to provide limited forensic artifacts under NDA and subject to subprocessor constraints.

Proposed tiering (subject to incident classification process):
- Critical: incidents resulting in confirmed unauthorized exfiltration of PHI or large-scale PII exposure — initial notification within 24 hours of detection; interim timeline updates every 24 hours; forensic snapshot delivery (sanitized) within 5 business days under NDA.
- High: confirmed unauthorized access to PII but no evidence of PHI exfiltration — initial notification within 48 hours; artifacts (logs/traces) delivered within 10 business days.
- Medium/Low: incidents limited to system stability or anomalies with no confirmed data exposure — notification within 72 hours; standard incident report on resolution.

Evidence sharing constraints and process:
- Redwood will provide forensically-sound, sanitized logs, request traces, and relevant system-level metadata where available. We will not provide raw disk images or raw memory dumps; where such artifacts are held by subprocessors or cloud providers, Redwood will (a) request cooperative assistance and (b) provide an attestation of steps taken if direct provision is not possible.
- Delivery will be under a mutual NDA or confidentiality addendum that specifies retention limits and permitted use (security analysis only).
- Cross-border transfer: any transfer of artifacts outside the EEA will be limited to the minimum necessary and comply with SCCs/appropriate transfer mechanism; we will notify NexusHealth of the destination and, if required, seek prior consent for transfers involving PHI.

Suggested redline snippet for the DPA (short form):
"""
For incidents classified as Critical or High, Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer with preserved and sanitized forensic artifacts and a written incident timeline within the timeframes set forth in Schedule X. Where artifacts cannot be disclosed due to third-party subprocessors or export controls, Provider shall (i) request cooperation from the subprocessors, (ii) provide Customer with a signed attestation of the steps taken, and (iii) escalate to Provider's senior security contacts. All artifact transfers shall be subject to a mutual NDA and limited to security analysis.
"""

Attachments referenced: proposed-notify-clause.txt (plain text redline), mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (word draft with rollout & operational tasks). Please review and let me know what Nexus needs changed.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-notify-clause.txt, mutual-action-plan-draft.docx

From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@nexushealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana.lee@counselfirm.com>, NexusHealth Security <security@nexushealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tailored notification windows + evidence access for NexusHealth

Thanks Neha — that helps a lot and is closer to what our team expects. A few follow-ups from Nexus:

1) For critical incidents, 5 business days for sanitized forensic artifacts is reasonable, provided those artifacts include (where available) web server request logs, API gateway traces, auth logs, and any relevant object store access logs. Can you confirm those item types are included in your definition of "sanitized logs"?

2) On subprocessors: Nexus will want an explicit escalation path if a subprocessor refuses to cooperate or claims they cannot provide artifacts due to their own contractual or export restrictions. Would Redwood be willing to commit to an SLA to escalate to Redwood's legal/security leadership within 48 hours of such a block?

3) Cross-border transfers: our counsel would like to see a clause that requires prior notice and explicit consent if PHI artifact transfers outside the EEA are necessary.

We opened a quick internal DocuSign review for the mutual NDA and I'll link it if/when it's ready. I've attached the Nexus intake form again for reference.

Regards,
Alex

Attachment: Nexus_Req_Form.pdf

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-16T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tailored notification windows + evidence access for NexusHealth

Alex — appreciate the quick follow. Final position from Redwood operations & legal below; happy to put this into a DPA addendum for sign-off.

1) Artifact scope: confirmed — when available we will provide web server request logs, API gateway traces, auth logs, object-store access logs and relevant application traces. All artifacts will be sanitized to remove unrelated customer data and delivered with a chain-of-custody note.

2) Subprocessors & escalation SLA: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain artifacts from subprocessors. If a subprocessor refuses or is unable to provide artifacts, Redwood will escalate to Redwood's security lead and legal within 48 hours of receiving the refusal and will notify Nexus within the same 48-hour window. We can commit to documenting escalation steps in the mutual action plan (Jira INC-4923 will be opened to track the subprocessor request lifecycle).

3) Cross-border transfers: Redwood will not transfer PHI-containing artifacts outside the EEA without prior written consent from Nexus (consent may be provided by email to the designated security contact). For non-PHI artifacts, Redwood will rely on SCCs or equivalent safeguards and will notify Nexus of the destination region.

Next steps:
- I'll have legal produce a short addendum that implements Neha's redlines plus the subprocessor escalation SLA.
- We'll attach a sample chain-of-custody template and our SOC 2 summary for Nexus to review.
- Laura will create the Jira ticket INC-4923 and link it to the mutual-action-plan draft.

Links/attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, link to Drive with chain-of-custody template: https://drive.redwood.com/share/forensic-evidence-protocol

If that aligns, we can have a redline to you by EOD Friday for Nexus counsel to review.

Best regards,
